packageRules.description: ADR-0059 §3: minor and patch arrive as one weekly pull request.

ADR-0059 §3: majors stay one per dependency, so a breaking change is read on its own and reverted on its own. Deliberately not behind dashboard approval — nothing merges because it is newer, and the gate on the PR is the whole argument, which a PR that never opens never reaches.

ADR-0059 §3 as carried by ADR-0073 §7, the pinning rule: exact for the runtime framework and the compiler, caret for everything else. `express` and its `@types` move together or the type surface describes a version that is not installed; `typescript` is exact because `tsc -b` writes the declaration output every other package type-checks against (ADR-0062 §3), and a patch that changes inference would move seventeen packages at once. `@vitest/coverage-v8` is exact for a reason the package itself states: its peer on `vitest` is an exact version rather than a range, so the pair has to arrive in one pull request — and with `autoInstallPeers` on in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, a provider left behind on an unsatisfiable peer is answered by a second copy of vitest rather than by a loud failure. Nothing else is pinned — this rule is the answer to "why these and not the rest", and a new exact pin belongs here with its reason or not at all. `rangeStrategy: pin` keeps Renovate proposing the next exact version rather than widening the range.

ADR-0073 §7, the one exception to the caret rule and the register of why it exists: `jsdom` is held below 30.1.0. That release rewrote the DOM tree, CSS and HTML-collection internals, and under it a Radix dropdown opened in a second `renderApp` of the same customer test file never mounts its menu — fourteen tests in four files time out on `findByRole("menu")`, each of them green on 30.0.1 and green on 30.1.0 when run alone. It is an upstream incompatibility rather than a defect in this tree, so the version is held with its reproduction rather than the suites rewritten around it. The hold itself is `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s `overrides` entry (ADR-0074 §2), which binds the resolution — vitest's auto-installed peer included — where this rule binds only what Renovate proposes. The two state the same version, exactly — a range here would let Renovate propose a 30.0.x the override then installs back to 30.0.1, a pull request that changes the manifests and nothing that runs. Lift both together by taking a later jsdom and running `pnpm test:unit --filter customer` whole.

ADR-0073 §4 and §7, the register's second hold (`D21.4`): `@types/node` stays on the runtime floor's major. The types major tracks the Node major, so 24's types describe the floor the tree runs on (`.nvmrc`, `engines`, the three Dockerfiles) and a newer major's describe APIs that floor does not have — a call they admit is a crash on the Node that ships. `pnpm outdated` listing the newer major is therefore the floor working, not a major left behind. The hold itself is `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s `overrides` entry (ADR-0074 §2), which binds the optional peers no manifest declares; this rule binds what Renovate proposes, and both name the same major. Lift both — and the catalog entry — in the pull request that moves the floor.

ADR-0073 §7: the base images the Dockerfiles and the compose files pin — `node` (three Dockerfiles), `nginx` (both SPA images), `postgres` (both compose files and the two workflows' service container) and `axllent/mailpit` (local compose and the e2e workflow). The default managers detect them; without this rule they arrive ungrouped and unlabelled, which is how a base image quietly stops being read. A major here is a runtime floor move (ADR-0073 §4) and stays its own pull request — which is why this rule names its update types rather than matching everything: Renovate applies `packageRules` in order and the last match wins per field, so an unrestricted rule here would have re-grouped the majors the rule above deliberately un-groups.
